data.title: NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns
data.description:
NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns

NSSF Challenges Maryland's Unconstitutional Ban on Popular Striker-Fired Handguns

PR Newswire

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026

WASHINGTON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- NSSF®, The Firearm Industry Trade Association, filed a lawsuit challenging Maryland's ban on popular cruciform-trigger handguns. Maryland Gov. Wes Moore signed S.B. 334 prohibiting the sale of these commonly owned firearms in the state earlier this year. The misguided law unconstitutionally infringes on the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding Maryland residents by prohibiting an entire class of lawfully made and sold handguns.

NSSF is pursuing a challenge to a similar unconstitutional law in Connecticut and recently secured a preliminary injunction barring enforcement of that law before it went into effect.

Maryland's law targeting "convertible pistols" infringes on the right of citizens to purchase the most-popular-selling handguns that are used for self-defense and renowned for their reliability. Maryland is unconstitutionally infringing on Second Amendment rights while ignoring criminals who violate federal and state law to illegally modify these handguns by attaching a "machinegun conversion device," or MCD, which has long been illegal to both make, import, possess or to attach to a firearm outside of strict federal licensing. The firearm industry warns gun owners against illegal modifications that override intentional semiautomatic firearm engineering designs. Illegally modifying a firearm to enable automatic fire is a federal and state crime. NSSF also strongly believes it's the Second Amendment right of firearm industry members suing Maryland to engage in lawful commerce by selling to law-abiding Americans the commonly used firearms they choose to acquire and which are protected by the constitution.

"To borrow on a line from James Carville, whom Democrats revere, 'it's the criminal, stupid,'" said Lawrence G. Keane, NSSF's Senior Vice President & General Counsel. "This law, and similar laws passed in other states, punishes law-abiding citizens by infringing on their Second Amendment rights to legally obtain the firearms they choose to protect themselves and their families against criminals who, by definition, have no respect for life or law. Instead of enforcing the law and holding these criminals accountable, Maryland's elected officials pander to gun control donors and antigun special interests to scapegoat the industry and ban an entire class of ordinary firearms, which the U.S. Supreme Court's Heller decision clearly holds violates the U.S. Constitution. Governor Moore knew this yet didn't hesitate to trample on the Second Amendment."

Under Maryland's S.B. 334, the ban includes pistols with a cruciform trigger bar that Maryland lawmakers say can be readily illegally converted by replacing the slide backplate with an illegal MCD. The ban is set to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

NSSF is joined in this lawsuit by the following NSSF member companies: GLOCK, Inc., Shadow Systems LLC, Sturm, Ruger & Co., Inc., Derya USA, Palmetto State Armory, LLC and Fred's Outdoors, LLC.

NSSF warns gun owners to stay on the "Right Side of LegalTM" when making improvements or customizing firearms. The Firearm Industry Trade Association warns that modifying a firearm by adding an illegal device that overrides the original, intended function or design to render a semiautomatic firearm into an automatic firearm is a felony. That includes importing, possessing, making or selling an MCD. It's a violation of the National Firearms Act (NFA) and carries a prison sentence of up to 10 years and up to $250,000 in fines.

About NSSF
NSSF is the trade association for the firearm industry. Its mission is to promote, protect and preserve hunting and the shooting sports. Formed in 1961, NSSF has a membership of thousands of manufacturers, distributors, firearms retailers, shooting ranges, sportsmen's organizations and publishers nationwide. For more information, visit nssf.org.

data.title: Court Grants Final Approval to Roundup™ Class Settlement
data.description:
Court Grants Final Approval to Roundup™ Class Settlement

  • Class settlement and the U.S. Supreme Court ruling are mutually reinforcing pillars in multi-pronged strategy to significantly contain the litigation
  • Monsanto will continue to vigorously defend cases and apply the Durnell ruling

Today, a Missouri state court granted final approval of the U.S. nationwide class settlement designed to resolve current and future Roundup™ claims alleging non-Hodgkin's lymphoma (NHL) injuries through a long-term claims program. The Court’s final approval order is subject to appeal. The class settlement, combined with the U.S. Supreme Court’s favorable ruling in June in the Durnell case, are mutually reinforcing pillars in the company’s multipronged strategy designed to significantly contain the Roundup™ litigation.

“The Court's final approval is a decisive milestone in the company's strategy to mitigate the risks of both pending and future Roundup™ litigation,” said Bill Anderson, CEO at Bayer.

The class approval decision follows closely on the heels of the unanimous defense verdict in Aretino, the first case to go to trial since the U.S. Supreme Court’s Durnell decision. Plaintiffs failed to prove design defect, fraud and negligence claims at trial, after the Court ruled their failure-to-warn claims were preempted by Durnell. This result validates Monsanto’s argument that these claims cannot be proven given that EPA and every other major regulatory body worldwide that has assessed such products, has found they can be used safely and are not carcinogenic. Glyphosate-based herbicides are critical tools that farmers rely on to produce affordable food and feed the world.

The company expects the number of opt outs to be manageable and amount to a very low percentage of current and potential future claims. Further, while a portion of the opt out claimants may pursue claims through the court system, many may not. Any plaintiff who chooses to litigate will face the burdens of both establishing that they have viable claims post-Durnell and ultimately proving them to a judge and jury. Monsanto believes the company is adequately provisioned to manage the remaining litigation.

About the class program

Monsanto pursued the class settlement to significantly contain the litigation, and the settlement agreement does not contain any admission of liability or wrongdoing. The Supreme Court ruling should foreclose any present or future claims based on failure-to-warn theories, the central theory in the litigation to date, including claims by opt outs from the class. The class settlement, in turn, provides a long-term claims program that will resolve present and future NHL injury claims, regardless of the legal theory on which they are based.

To fund the class settlement, Monsanto will make declining capped annual payments for up to 21 years totaling up to 7.25 billion U.S. dollars, inclusive of payments already made. The long-term payment stream will provide both greater certainty and control regarding litigation costs for current claims and future claimants.

The settlement includes plaintiffs who allege exposure to Roundup™ prior to February 17, 2026, and:

  • have a medical diagnosis of NHL now; or
  • receive a medical diagnosis of NHL before the end of a 16-year period following the effective date of the agreement.

Any appeal of the Court’s final approval order would pause further Monsanto payments until such appeals are exhausted. Monsanto believes the Court’s thoughtful and well-reasoned final approval order provides a very strong foundation supporting the class settlement, if the approval order is appealed, and the company will work together with class counsel to defend any challenges.

Find more information at www.bayer.com.

data.title: Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips
data.description:
Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips

Mendez & Sanchez Finds Three Counties Accounted for Nearly Two-Thirds of California Rideshare Trips

PR Newswire

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 20, 2026

The firm's review of 2019–2020 collision and trip data highlights the need for bilingual insurance guidance in California's largest rideshare markets.

LOS ANGELES, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- A Mendez & Sanchez APC review of California rideshare records found that Los Angeles, San Francisco and San Diego counties accounted for nearly two-thirds of the state's rideshare trips from September 2019 through August 2020. For passengers in Los Angeles and San Diego counties, both home to large Latino communities, the firm says access to bilingual information can make a difference when a crash raises questions about insurance.

"This is not about saying Latino passengers are inherently more likely to be injured in a rideshare crash," said Michael Sanchez, co-founder and managing partner at Mendez & Sanchez APC. "It is about recognizing that rideshare collision exposure is concentrated in counties where millions of Latino and Spanish-speaking residents live, work and use app-based transportation. That makes access to clear legal information in English and Spanish especially important."

The firm reviewed the San Francisco County Transportation Authority's analysis of reports filed by Uber and Lyft. The authority counted nearly 27,000 reported collisions statewide during the 12-month period. Uber reported about 14,800 collisions and Lyft about 11,200. Comparing those figures with subsequent years is difficult because the California Public Utilities Commission suspended the requirement that companies submit public versions of their 2021 through 2024 annual reports.

"Passengers deserve transparency," said Sanchez. "If someone is injured in an Uber or Lyft crash, they should not have to guess what insurance applies, what evidence they need to save or whether they have the right to pursue a claim."

California's Senate Bill 371 changed the coverage required when another driver causes a crash and has little or no insurance. While a passenger is in the rideshare vehicle, the required uninsured and underinsured motorist coverage is now $60,000 per person and $300,000 per incident, down from $1 million. A separate $1 million liability requirement still applies when the rideshare driver causes a crash during the trip.

"Rideshare cases can be complicated because insurance coverage may depend on the driver's app status, the phase of the ride and who caused the crash," said Sanchez. "For Spanish-speaking families, those questions can feel even more overwhelming if no one explains the process clearly."

About Mendez & Sanchez, A.P.C.

Mendez & Sanchez represents individuals and families in serious injury and civil litigation matters in Southern California, Nevada and Honduras. The firm offers legal services in English and Spanish on a contingency-fee basis. It has handled more than 5,000 cases and recovered over $1 billion for clients. Learn more at www.mendezsanchezlaw.com.

Green Giant Canada Announces a Voluntary Recall of Certain Cans of Green Giant Cream Style Corn Manufactured by Nortera Foods Because of Possible Foreign Material

Green Giant Canada announced today that Nortera Foods, a third-party manufacturer, is voluntarily recalling certain 398 mL / 14 fl oz cans of Green Giant Cream Style Corn due to the potential for hard plastic to be present in the recalled product. Although neither Green Giant Canada nor Nortera Foods is aware of any hard plastic having been found in any finished product, the recall is being conducted as a preventive measure.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261120426010/en/

This recall applies only to the following products distributed in Canada and bearing the “best before” dates specified below:

(The “best before” date is located on the top of the can.)

This voluntary recall does not apply to any other “best before” dates, sizes or varieties of Green Giant products sold in Canada.

There have been no reports of injury or illness to date associated with the recalled product. However, in line with Green Giant Canada’s commitment to food safety and quality, Nortera Foods and we are taking action to remove the recalled product from the locations where it was distributed and to notify consumers. The recall is being conducted in cooperation with the Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA).

Consumers who have purchased the recalled product should not consume it and are urged to return it to the place of purchase for a refund. data.title: Allooloo Tops 100M Capital Markets AI Agent Traffic a Month
data.description:
Allooloo Tops 100M Capital Markets AI Agent Traffic a Month

Allooloo Tops 100M Capital Markets AI Agent Traffic a Month

PR Newswire

VANCOUVER, BC and LONDON, Nov. 20, 2026

Agentic datasets on every listed company in 34 countries: sourced, dated and signed.

VANCOUVER, BC and LONDON, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Allooloo Technologies Corp. (Allooloo), maker of agentic datasets for capital markets artificial intelligence (AI) agents, today reported 100M AI agent traffic a month. That is 39 calls a second, 3.4 million a day, across getissuer.ai and Issuerwire.ai, running on 24 Microsoft Azure hyperscale locations globally with always-on Amazon Web Services (AWS) redundancy.

The Data Readiness Gap

Investment banks are not short of AI models. They are short of data an AI agent can use. In a 2026 Teradata study, 77% of technology leaders said 20% or less of their enterprise data is ready for AI agents. Banks are closing that gap on the data they hold, with one governed way in and the source, the date and the owner on every record.

The data a bank does not hold is the other half. An AI agent working on a security needs the issuer, its disclosures and whether it may be ordered, in every market the bank trades. Allooloo delivers that half agent-ready: 41.9K listed companies in 34 countries, a source and a date on every field, and a signed receipt for every read, over Model Context Protocol (MCP).

Two Products

Know Your Product (KYP) is the duty to know a security before it is recommended or sold. Allooloo KYP, at getissuer.ai, answers it for the AI agent: who the issuer is, whether it may be ordered, and who it is for. It covers 41.9K listed companies on 79 exchanges in 34 countries.

Issuerwire.ai is the dated disclosure wire: 3.1 million dated disclosures across 34 countries, each with its source.

Who it matters to:

  • Investment bank or dealer: its AI agents can show where each fact came from.
  • The issuer: every AI agent reads the same answer about it.
  • Compliance: a signed receipt for every cleared read.

A Signed Receipt for Every Read

Every cleared read on Allooloo leaves a signed receipt, the Record of Cleared Orders (RCO): what was read, when, and under which market's rules.

Each Market in Its Own Country

Each market is kept in its own country or region, across 24 Microsoft Azure regions, on one MCP server per market. A second copy of every market is made each night on AWS and locked against deletion for 365 days. Allooloo is a Microsoft AI Cloud Partner.

Around the Clock

The products are made around the clock by Allooloo's own team and AI agents, on the Allooloo Algo. AI agents call them around the clock and pay per call, with no seat and no licence.

"Today we are announcing a milestone: 100M AI agent traffic a month," said Matthew Keddy, Chief Executive Officer of Allooloo Technologies Corp. "These are the AI agents of capital markets participants, and they want crisp data, five years deep, on 41.9K listed companies across 79 exchanges: sourced, dated and signed. Gain the edge with us."

In Session and Enterprise Grade

Allooloo is sold two ways. In session, an AI agent calls Allooloo mid-task and pays as it goes (PayGo) on x402, the open payment standard for AI agents, with no seat and no licence. At enterprise grade, a firm licenses the datasets to design, build and run its own AI agents.

About Allooloo Technologies Corp.

Allooloo Technologies Corp. makes agentic capital markets data products for the AI agents of banks, dealers and issuers. Its products, getissuer.ai and Issuerwire.ai, cover 41.9K listed companies on 79 exchanges in 34 countries, kept across 24 Microsoft Azure regions with on-the-fly redundancy on Amazon Web Services (AWS). The result is always-on agentic datasets: in session for AI lab users, and enterprise grade for customers who design, build and run their own AI agents. Allooloo is headquartered in Vancouver, Canada. Please visit: allooloo.ai

data.title: RxERP Outlines What the FDA’s Move to 12-Digit NDCs Means for Pharma Product Data
data.description:
RxERP Outlines What the FDA’s Move to 12-Digit NDCs Means for Pharma Product Data

New overview and checklist help teams review product matching, barcode data, and trading-partner workflows ahead of the 2033 change

RxERP, the serialized enterprise resource planning platform purpose-built for the pharmaceutical supply chain, today released a 12-Digit NDC readiness overview and companion checklist to help pharmaceutical companies prepare their product records and workflows for the FDA’s new 12-digit NDC format. The resources build on RxERP’s support for 10-, 11-, and 12-digit representations of a product’s NDC within one product record, helping manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, and 3PLs keep product identity consistent as formats change.

The operational challenge begins when trading partners identify the same product differently. A supplier’s code may fail to match the version stored in the receiving system, requiring a manual lookup or prompting creation of a duplicate item. Those duplicates can split inventory counts, lot history, and pricing across records. Adding a new NDC format makes reliable product matching essential across receiving, inventory, orders, and traceability data.

Under the FDA’s final rule, the uniform 12-digit NDC takes effect March 7, 2033, with a labeling transition through March 6, 2036. The rule itself leaves HIPAA standards unchanged, while the FDA expects billing standards to accommodate 12 digits by 2033.

The transition also changes how systems connect National Drug Codes with Global Trade Item Numbers, or GTINs, used in serialized workflows. The existing NDC-based GTIN structure cannot embed a 12-digit NDC. Software that extracts an NDC from a GTIN will therefore need to change how it associates the identifiers with the correct product and packaging level. GS1 application identifier 715 provides a way to carry the NDC as a separate barcode data element alongside the GTIN.

“A product shouldn’t become two products because a trading partner sent its NDC in a different format,” said Steve Madsen, founder and CEO of RxERP. “We connect those NDC formats to one product record so teams can maintain a consistent product identity. These resources help companies identify the remaining work across barcodes, integrations, and trading partners while they have time to plan and test.”

The overview explains the conversion rules, the GTIN mapping challenge, and actions for manufacturers, repackagers, distributors, 3PLs, and pharmacies. The companion checklist turns that guidance into a working assessment, with space to record test results, document evidence, assign owners, and set follow-up dates. Teams can use it to test whether their systems can:

  • Match original and converted NDCs to the correct product and package record while preserving strength, dosage form, and package differences.
  • Preserve leading zeros and handle newly assigned 12-digit NDCs without misclassifying them as UPCs.
  • Interpret GS1 AI (715) through both the scanner and receiving application while continuing to process existing barcodes.
  • Exchange identifiers correctly with trading partners and follow a product through receiving, inventory, an outbound order, and serialized-data workflows.

RxERP brings product records, serialized data, inventory, and orders into the same platform, with serialization built into operational workflows. Its FDA NDC API integration brings FDA product data into the item master, and product setup draws on FDA and GS1 data to reduce manual entry. Keeping NDC representations associated with one product record provides a foundation for the broader barcode and trading-partner work required by the transition.

Read the 12-Digit NDC overview and download the working checklist at https://rxerp.com/12-digit-ndc-transition/

About RxERP

RxERP is a purpose-built, fully serialized pharmaceutical ERP that unifies financial management, inventory, distribution, warehouse operations, customer ordering, DSCSA compliance, and EPCIS traceability within one integrated platform. RxERP helps pharmaceutical manufacturers, wholesalers, distributors, 3PL providers, and pharmacies expanding into distribution streamline operations, to reduce manual processes, support compliance workflows, and scale with greater visibility and control.
